evidence.observation: The literal search/replace strategy. It computes `num = original_text.count(search_text)`, but the ambiguity guard is commented out (`# if num > 1: #    raise SearchTextNotUnique()`); the only live guard is `if num == 0: return`. It then calls `original_text.replace(search_text, replace_text)` with no count argument, so an ambiguous (multi-occurrence) search_text is silently expanded to EVERY occurrence rather than failing. This is the normalized operation result of the ambiguity contract at this call site.

`class SearchTextNotUnique(ValueError)` is the repository's marker exception for an ambiguous SEARCH side. It is defined here but never raised by `search_and_replace` (the raise is commented out), so the ambiguity failure contract is only enforced elsewhere (e.g. the udiff coder catches it). Naming this symbol grounds the claim that search_replace.py owns the ambiguity-signal type without enforcing it in the literal strategy.

Handles `...` elision in an edit block. It splits the SEARCH and REPLACE into pieces and, for each non-empty piece, `if whole.count(part) == 0: raise ValueError` and `if whole.count(part) > 1: raise ValueError`. The `> 1` branch is the focused ambiguous-match failure: an ambiguous SEARCH piece is refused instead of guessed, and only a unique piece is applied via `whole.replace(part, replace, 1)`.

The edit-block entry point that turns the ambiguous-match guard into a normalized failure result. It tries a perfect/whitespace-tolerant match, then wraps `try_dotdotdots` in `try: ... except ValueError: pass`, and after the disabled fuzzy fallback returns `None`. Consequence: when `try_dotdotdots` raises on an ambiguous piece, `replace_most_similar_chunk` returns `None` (no edit applied), which `do_replace` and `EditBlockCoder.apply_edits` surface as a SearchReplaceNoExactMatch failure.

claims.claim: search_replace.py defines the ambiguity signal but does not enforce it in its literal strategy: search_and_replace computes `num = original_text.count(search_text)` yet the `if num > 1: raise SearchTextNotUnique()` guard is commented out, so it calls `str.replace` without a count and rewrites every occurrence of an ambiguous SEARCH; SearchTextNotUnique exists solely as the marker exception type for this case.

Edit-block handling enforces a focused ambiguous-match failure: in try_dotdotdots a `...` SEARCH piece that matches more than one location raises ValueError (`whole.count(part) > 1`), replace_most_similar_chunk swallows that ValueError and returns None, so the edit is reported as failed instead of silently editing an arbitrary occurrence.

tests/basic/test_editblock.py now contains a focused ambiguous-match failure case (test_replace_ambiguous_match_with_ellipsis_fails) asserting the edit-block matcher returns None for an ambiguous `...` piece, paired with test_replace_unambiguous_match_with_ellipsis_succeeds for the unique case and the pre-existing test_replace_multiple_matches documenting that a plain duplicate SEARCH replaces only the first occurrence.

The ambiguity contract differs between the two entry points: the edit-block path (editblock_coder.try_dotdotdots -> replace_most_similar_chunk) fails on an ambiguous `...` piece, whereas search_replace.search_and_replace deliberately (guard commented out) rewrites all occurrences; both files therefore participate in defining the end-to-end ambiguous-match behavior.

conclusion: Contract established and demonstrated for ambiguous search/replace matches in aider. The edit-block matcher refuses to guess: an ambiguous `...` SEARCH piece triggers ValueError in try_dotdotdots, which replace_most_similar_chunk converts to a None result that apply_edits reports as a SearchReplaceNoExactMatch failure, while a unique piece still applies. A focused failure case (test_replace_ambiguous_match_with_ellipsis_fails) plus its unambiguous mirror were added to tests/basic/test_editblock.py, alongside the pre-existing test_replace_multiple_matches that documents first-occurrence behavior for plain duplicates. Separately, aider/coders/search_replace.py's literal search_and_replace strategy leaves its SearchTextNotUnique ambiguity guard commented out, so it rewrites every occurrence; SearchTextNotUnique is the marker exception for that case. The contract is executable via .prale-eval/demo_ambiguous_match.py, which runs the real extracted functions with the standard library only.
